facts.statement: Lusovenator is a genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Lusovenator (meaning "Portuguese hunter") is a genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: The genus Lusovenator contains only one known species, Lusovenator santosi.
facts.quote: It includes one species, Lusovenator santosi.

facts.statement: Lusovenator fossils have been found in the Lourinhã Formation in present-day Portugal.
facts.quote: from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Praia de Amoreira Porto-Novo Member and the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous (Tithonian-Berriasian) Assenta Member of the Lourinhã Formation in present-day Portugal

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the 1980s by José Joaquim dos Santos.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered during the 1980s by José Joaquim dos Santos

facts.statement: The discoverer donated the fossil collection to the Sociedade de História Natural approximately thirty years after finding it.
facts.quote: he donated his fossil collection to the Sociedade de História Natural around thirty years later

facts.statement: The holotype was initially described and classified within Allosauroidea in 2017.
facts.quote: The unnamed holotype was described and placed in the Allosauroidea in 2017

facts.statement: A neotype was described in 2019, and both the holotype and neotype were subsequently placed within Carcharodontosauria.
facts.quote: The neotype, was described in 2019 and both specimens were placed within Carcharodontosauria

facts.statement: The species name Lusovenator santosi was formally named and described in 2020.
facts.quote: The species Lusovenator santosi was named and described in 2020

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial postcranial skeleton including vertebrae, ribs, and pelvic fragments, thought to represent a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: The known remains consist of the holotype SHN.036 - "a partial postcranial skeleton preserving the odontoid, the atlantal intercentrum, a cervical vertebra, isolated cervical neural spines, dorsal vertebrae, fragments of sacral vertebrae, caudal vertebrae, chevrons, fragments of cervical and dorsal ribs, the right ilium, both pubes, and ischia"

facts.statement: The genus name combines 'Lusitania' (ancient Portugal) and 'venator' (hunter), meaning 'Portuguese hunter'.
facts.quote: The generic name Lusovenator is derived from Lusitania, the province of the Roman Empire that roughly matches present-day Portugal, affixed with the Latin venator, meaning "hunter"

facts.statement: The species name 'santos' honors the discoverer, José Joaquim dos Santos.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, santosi, refers to José Joaquim dos Santos, who discovered the remains

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Lusovenator within Carcharodontosauria but outside the families Carcharodontosauridae and Neovenatoridae.
facts.quote: The describers ran a phylogenetic analysis and recovered Lusovenator within the clade Carcharodontosauria, outside Carcharodontosauridae and Neovenatoridae

facts.statement: A 2024 study by Cau suggests Lusovenator belongs to the family Carcharodontosauridae, grouping it with Sauroniops, Veterupristisaurus, Eocarcharia, and Concavenator.
facts.quote: Cau (2024) found Lusovenator to be in the family Carcharodontosauridae, forming a clade with Sauroniops, Veterupristisaurus, Eocarcharia, and Concavenator

facts.statement: Lusovenator lived between 152.21 and 143.1 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 143.1 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A referred specimen includes a series of articulated caudal vertebrae and an almost complete right foot.
rejected.quote: and the referred specimen SHN.019, "a partial skeleton represented by a series of articulated caudal vertebrae and an almost complete right pes"
